anti_overlap: Leave the three-budget decision tree itself to fd-gambian-jaliya-trio-tuning
Focus on instrument-vs-sample distinction, not on the choice rule
decision_lens: Is the null model genuinely inert — does it truly spend zero attention — or does the harness itself cause attention spend through observation overhead, tick-loop side effects, or implicit actions? If the vessel is not inert, calibration measures the instrument, not the model.
distance_rationale: A centuries-old shrine-brewery technique for proving wild-yeast vs vessel contamination — structurally a zero-input control for apparatus validation, distant from software but directly isomorphic to null-baseline instrument certification.
expected_isomorphisms: The unpitched control tank corresponds to the null model; any activity in the control tank invalidates the pitched-tank measurement. Likewise any attention spend by the null invalidates the budget floor calibration.
focus: Running the null baseline as a parallel-ferment control that certifies the measurement apparatus itself is inert, borrowing the bodai-moto yeast-starter tradition of fermenting an unpitched control tank alongside the real starter to prove spontaneous activity comes from the wild yeast and not from the vessel.
name: fd-sake-bodai-moto-parallel-ferment
persona: Apply the perspective of a toji (master sake brewer) trained in the bodai-moto (bodai-style yeast starter) tradition at a Nara shrine brewery — they care about whether the 'null vessel' (unpitched water+rice) shows any fermentation, they measure acidity and gas evolution over days in both the seeded and unseeded tank, and they flag when the control tank shows ANY activity because that means the vessel itself contributes flavor and invalidates the experiment. Here the 'vessel' is shadowbench-runner and the 'control tank' is the null model.
review_areas: Whether scripted::null has any code path that invokes try_spend, observe(), or act() — the control tank must be dry
Whether the harness (runner, trace emitters, /bench endpoints) causes AttentionBudget mutation independent of model policy
Whether 'null model spends 0' is a property verified by assertion, not merely by naming — the risk #2 in the brainstorm is unresolved
Whether observation_budget and action_budget (v0.2 dual-budget fields) leak into v0.1 AttentionBudget accounting and confound the null
Whether the pre-pilot tarball captures a hash of the runner binary and sim binary so the 'inert vessel' claim is reproducible

severity_examples.condition: Every 'non-binding' verdict at B=5 would actually measure null-spend rate, not null-floor — the calibration is a null-policy measurement, not an instrument calibration
severity_examples.scenario: scripted::null calls a default observe() that decrements AttentionBudget by 1 per tick

severity_examples.condition: Apparatus-induced spend indistinguishable from model spend; all three levels appear non-binding but for the wrong reason
severity_examples.scenario: The trace emitter for year boundaries calls a debug hook that logs attention snapshots by invoking try_spend(0) which still ticks an internal counter

success_hints: Grep for any call site of try_spend / decrement_attention reachable from the null-model execution path
Require a unit test that asserts AttentionBudget.remaining == per_year at every tick for the null model
Recommend a 'spend_policy: inert' tag on the null model so the inertness is a typed property, not a naming convention
task_context: The calibration relies on the null model being a true floor. A bodai-moto-style apparatus audit asks whether the instrument itself is inert before trusting the floor reading.
